name: SQuAD (Stanford Question Answering Dataset) v1.0
description: A reading comprehension dataset consisting of 100,000+ questions posed by crowdworkers on a set of Wikipedia articles, where the answer to each question is a segment of text from the corresponding reading passage.

creator.name: Pranav Rajpurkar, Jian Zhang, Konstantin Lopyrev, Percy Liang

citeAs: Pranav Rajpurkar, Jian Zhang, Konstantin Lopyrev, and Percy Liang. 2016. SQuAD: 100,000+ Questions for Machine Comprehension of Text. arXiv:1606.05250v3 [cs.CL]
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected in three stages: (1) curating passages from Wikipedia articles, (2) crowdsourcing question-answer pairs on those passages, and (3) obtaining additional answers for evaluation purposes.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Over the development and test sets, 2.6% of questions were marked unanswerable by at least one of the additional crowdworkers.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Wikipedia articles were retrieved using Project Nayuki's Wikipedia's internal PageRanks to obtain the top 10000 articles of English Wikipedia, from which 536 articles were sampled uniformly at random. From each article, individual paragraphs were extracted, stripping away images, figures, tables, and discarding paragraphs shorter than 500 characters. The result was 23,215 paragraphs for the 536 articles covering a wide range of topics.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Paragraphs were extracted from Wikipedia articles, stripping away images, figures, tables, and discarding paragraphs shorter than 500 characters. The articles were partitioned randomly into a training set (80%), a development set (10%), and a test set (10%).
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Individual paragraphs were extracted from Wikipedia articles, stripping away images, figures, tables, and discarding paragraphs shorter than 500 characters.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdworkers were tasked with asking and answering up to 5 questions on the content of each paragraph. Questions had to be entered in a text field, and answers had to be highlighted in the paragraph. Workers were encouraged to ask questions in their own words, without copying word phrases from the paragraph. Copy-paste functionality on the paragraph text was disabled. Workers were asked to spend 4 minutes on every paragraph. For additional answers, crowdworkers were shown only the questions along with the paragraphs and asked to select the shortest span in the paragraph that answered the question. If a question was not answerable by a span in the paragraph, workers were asked to submit the question without marking an answer.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Daemo platform, with Amazon Mechanical Turk as its backend
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: To get an indication of human performance on SQuAD and to make evaluation more robust, at least 2 additional answers were obtained for each question in the development and test sets. Human performance was assessed by treating the second answer to each question as the human prediction, and keeping the other answers as ground truth answers. The resulting human performance score on the test set is 77.0% for the exact match metric, and 86.8% for F1. Mismatch occurs mostly due to inclusion/exclusion of non-essential phrases rather than fundamental disagreements about the answer.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each question in the development and test sets has at least 3 answers (1 original answer plus at least 2 additional answers)
rai:annotatorDemographics: Crowdworkers were required to have a 97% HIT acceptance rate, a minimum of 1000 HITs, and be located in the United States or Canada.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford CoreNLP was used to generate constituency parses, POS tags, dependency parse trees, and NER tags for dataset analysis and feature extraction.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is freely available at https://stanford-qa.com. The paper describes SQuAD v1.0. All code, data, and experiments are available on the CodaLab platform.
rai:dataLimitations: The span constraint means that 77.3% of the correct answers in the development set are constituents in the constituency parse, placing an effective ceiling on the accuracy of methods that only consider constituents as candidate answers. The dataset focuses on questions whose answers are entailed by the passage, which is more constrained than interpretative questions found in more advanced standardized tests. Some questions (2.6% in dev/test sets) were marked unanswerable by at least one crowdworker.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for training and evaluating reading comprehension systems. It can be used for Training, Testing, and Validation. The dataset was partitioned into a training set (80%), a development set (10%), and a test set (10%).
